html:
In May 1987 Lieutenant Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka seized parliament in Suva and overthrew the new government of Timoci Bavadra, backed mostly by Indo-Fijians. A second coup in September made Fiji a republic.

Rabuka said he acted to keep power in the hands of indigenous Fijians. A new constitution in 1990 reserved most seats and the top offices for them.

Tens of thousands of Indo-Fijians, descendants of the indenture workers, left for Australia, New Zealand and Canada in the years after. Fiji was suspended from the Commonwealth. Further coups followed in 2000 and 2006. See also Ratu Mara.
